- When sentiment is consistently negative or low (e.g., < 0.5), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to recent highs.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use 3-period moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.8 for 3+ days), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–3% to prevent overconfidence.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in downward trends; if recent 5-day average is 5% below 30-day average, adjust forecast to align with 30-day trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7), model often lags; add 1–2 days of lagged sentiment to forecast adjustment.
- When sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast by 5–10% if sentiment drops below 0.3 within 3 days.
